reviews.lens: Identity, evidence status, authorization and mutation recovery

findings.criterion: Write integrity under an unknown result
findings.observation: The assembled creation card can create a second Person after a real 201 receipt is lost and the note is edited. Pi's first unknown-result patch is not integrated; review also found unvalidated receipts and stale-scope continuation.
findings.evidence: Artifact 9938d394; evidence/create-lost-response-duplicate.json records two distinct Person IDs; frontend-third-review.txt in the private task evidence holds code-review reproduction points.
findings.user_impact: One human intent becomes two identities and fragmented source history, with uncertain ownership and no reliable recovery.
findings.recommendation: Keep exact immutable request/scope state until a matching receipt resolves it; block stale workspace continuations and warn before discarding recovery.
findings.verification: Lost-201 browser retry returns the original identity/resource; malformed/wrong-scope receipts and unmount/account races cause no new intent or follow-up write.

findings.observation: The resident relationship route rejects unchanged proposed evidence late. The local repair consistently excludes it from the reviewed manifest, while its final revocation check still passes the negative tests.
findings.user_impact: A normal pending-review state becomes a misleading conflict after provider work; users may repeatedly retry without understanding why.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the reviewed fix and repeat the affected real-browser journey before closing EXP-13.
findings.verification: Unchanged proposed evidence does not appear in reviewed model context and no longer triggers a fictitious source-change result; revoked evidence still blocks completion.

strengths: Source and Memory remain separate: imported unconfirmed source did not populate accepted Person Memory.
Source revision conflicts refresh once and require another explicit decision; deletion consent is reset.
missing_evidence: EXP-11 integrated code and real-backend retry acceptance.
Current runtime deployment/readback of EXP-09 and EXP-13.
Full derived-store and external integration deletion/reversal acceptance.
vetoes: Unknown-save recovery can duplicate a Person

reviews.lens: Responsive task legibility, visual craft, keyboard and interruption recovery

findings.observation: Creation still has an unresolved duplicate-write path in the assembled build. A visually successful form cannot pass the journey while a lost reply admits another Person.
findings.user_impact: The user cannot tell whether to edit, retry or open an already-saved Person after a connection interruption.
findings.recommendation: Complete and browser-test the pending/unknown/committed state model before accepting the visual improvements.
findings.verification: The recovery notice is focused and visible at 320px; exact-request replay produces one saved identity; navigation can be safely declined.

findings.observation: Measured form contrast, responsive geometry and keyboard skip behavior cover bounded surfaces. Native browser enlargement, assistive technology and production performance remain unverified.
findings.user_impact: Users with larger text or assistive technology may encounter barriers not visible in ordinary screenshots; source admission already caused whole-API stalls.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these deductions and collect production-runtime, browser-enlargement and assistive-technology evidence.
findings.verification: Critical tasks complete with the required access modes and interruption states; latency checks run against the deployed revision.

strengths: Form labels/inputs now measure 14/16px and affected mobile controls meet 44px.
Shell primary labels measure 12px and all header targets meet 44px at 320/390/430px.
Creation entry focuses the visible name field; Time deletion uses a compact terminal state.
Solid-color form text passes the measured 4.5:1 criterion in both themes.
missing_evidence: Full keyboard completion beyond the verified skip link and focused recovery notices.
Native browser zoom and assistive-technology user evidence.
Populated desktop and content-extreme visual retest after all integrated changes.
vetoes: Unknown-save recovery can duplicate a Person
open_questions: Does a narrow form with nested vertical scrolling remain understandable in a first-use task trial?

reviews.lens: Practical continuity from source capture to reviewed relationship state

findings.observation: A missing save receipt can fragment one contact-creation intent into two people. The known partial-success path is improved, but an unknown first result remains an active gate.
findings.user_impact: The operator must reconstruct what saved and which Person owns the evidence, adding work and risking incorrect follow-up.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the frozen intent explicitly before allowing corrections to become a new intent.
findings.verification: After an interrupted save, the user reaches one canonical Person with the expected note and clue, without duplicate creation.

findings.observation: Sources, relationship brief and Person Memory now have clearer labels, but successful imported source does not by itself prove a completed Memory-review loop. The attempted live Memory proposal failed and stayed retryable.
findings.evidence: README.md revised browser acceptance and coverage; Person ea7363d2-1f21-4686-bdbb-03210e7736dd in the isolated Lab; Session 5bc26235-ff8f-43fb-b86d-dcc315cc1802.
findings.user_impact: The user can inspect the source yet still lacks proof that a reviewed statement is saved, corrected and available from the Person destination.
findings.recommendation: Finish the real model proposal, per-item confirmation, destination reload and correction/undo loop; retain failure evidence separately.
findings.verification: A synthetic grounded proposal becomes exactly the selected accepted Memory item and reloads at the correct Person; correction/undo preserve provenance.

strengths: Real creation reaches its authenticated destination and retains one note plus one confirmed clue.
Source conflict preserves editable input and requires a fresh choice.
Conversation stop/edit/reload/continue and Time create/edit/delete lifecycle were exercised.
missing_evidence: Representative recruiter task trials and time-to-completion comparisons.
Successful live Memory-review lifecycle in this audit.
Cross-device/day recovery and exact-runtime prioritization acceptance.
vetoes: Unknown-save recovery can duplicate a Person
open_questions: Can a first-time operator explain source, brief and accepted Memory without visiting all three surfaces?

reviews.lens: Evaluation design audit; no assessment of candidate quality

findings.observation: The collected checks demonstrate individual synthetic state transitions; they do not establish a calibrated end-to-end experience score or human satisfaction.
findings.evidence: Artifact 9938d394 with resident backend 973e7913-platform; evidence/manifest.json; plans/2026-09-24-experience-98.md lists unverified native, latency and recovery gates.
findings.user_impact: An aggregate 98 claim could conceal duplicate writes, inaccessible states or provider failures.
findings.recommendation: Freeze atomic journey criteria, distinguish failures from missing evidence, and withhold the threshold claim while critical gates remain.
findings.verification: Every awarded point has a reproducible locator on the tested revision; no active critical gate is averaged away.

strengths: Synthetic fixtures are isolated from real relationship records.
Before/after PostgreSQL regressions and canonical browser readbacks distinguish mechanisms from visual opinion.
missing_evidence: Independent human task-comprehension and seeded-error trials.
Rater calibration or repeat/order stability for subjective craft judgments.
Full state/locale/device coverage and resident-runtime acceptance.
open_questions: Which user-observed outcomes should complement the internal technical scorecard after release gates pass?
